results.name: Opening, abandoning and discarding a plan never creates a business row or resurrects a discarded draft
Own interval and existing text phrases save offline on the original equipment
Today done requires explicit save, allows date and reason, and can shorten the next interval
One earlier date leaves the standing interval intact; permanent shortening sends different arguments
Lost commit reply survives reload and is resolved by read-back with the original ID, without a second write
A post-commit view read failure does not undo a completed maintenance
Write conflict preserves input and requires explicit comparison before saving against the new hash
Maintenance forms remain usable at narrow widths and enlarged text
Editing the existing interval preserves equipment, plan identity and completed history
An unknown current-session commit is read first, then explicitly retried with the same ID and arguments
An unknown restored action stays read-only and cannot replay automatically
